finding.title: Stop FirestoreGatewayImpl.pushGoal from using non-idempotent add() for id-less goals

evidence.quote:
final id = goal['id']?.toString() ?? goal['goal_id']?.toString();
    if (id != null) return id;

finding.why: Every other push* method here (pushCompletion, pushStreak, pushTrack, pushLedgerEntry...) derives a deterministic Firestore doc id so an outbox retry after a lost ack is a safe overwrite via set(merge:true). pushGoal is the one method that falls back to collection.add() -- a fresh random doc id -- whenever the payload carries no id/goal_id. outbox_sync_write_facade.dart's own _goalKey fallback (a composite curriculum_pct_timestamp key) proves this null case is real, not theoretical: it exists specifically to dedupe local enqueues of such goals. If the server commits the add() but the client never sees the ack (timeout, dropped connection -- exactly what the outbox's at-least-once retry exists to survive), the retry calls add() again and creates a second, permanent duplicate goal document in Firestore, which the pull path then merges back down as a duplicate goal locally.
finding.recommendation: Assign every goal a stable id before it is ever enqueued (mirror the ULID pattern already used for streak/ledger/points-ledger entries) and have pushGoal always do doc(id).set(merge:true); delete the add() branch.
acceptance_criteria: Regression test: call pushGoal twice with an id-less payload against a fake/emulator Firestore; assert exactly one document exists afterward.
pushGoal's add() branch is removed or provably unreachable.
